newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan president reveals personal wealth.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan president reveals personal wealth.

text.p: President Arnoldo Aleman on Monday became the first Nicaraguan head of state to reveal his personal wealth, unveiling a list of possessions showing he is a millionaire.

Aleman, 50, said his possessions were worth a total of $1.05 million and included four ranches, two houses, a small island, a coffee mill, part of two apartments in Miami, art worth $100,000, stocks, $40,000 in jewelry and eight vehicles, including a 1997 Mercedes Benz.
He also had 500 head of cattle and $63,653 in a bank account, his statement said. He said he had no debts.

Aleman, who took power on Jan. 10, presented the list to Comptroller General Augustin Jarquin and said that making public his wealth was proof that his right-wing government was committed to fighting corruption.
Officials in his government had done the same or would do so, he pledged.

"I've said the only revolution, both in Nicaragua and Latin America, is the revolution of honesty. So here I am to present this to the nation's controller general so that he has a clear, firm record of our belongings," Aleman told reporters.
Jarquin, whose job is to oversee government spending, said Aleman was the first president in history to declare his wealth publicly.
Former presidents Daniel Ortega and Violeta Chamorro never revealed their personal assets while in office.
Earlier, the Somoza family dictatorship ruled Nicaragua for nearly half a century, attaining considerable wealth through graft and corruption.
The final years of Chamorro's government were plagued by corruption scandals involving her appointees.
Aleman said about 90 percent of the incoming officials with his Liberal Alliance government had already filed official declarations of their wealth with Jarquin.
A CID-Gallup poll in December showed that more than 90 percent of Nicaraguans thought government corruption was a problem, and 40 percent thought Aleman's government would be corrupt.
